wsl-claude, on grantFace, as the tree stands after your revert (6630efb): the MAP ALREADY EXISTS, living in the wrong app. appFaceApp on your node keeps grants.json, where each row maps a name to a key and optionally an app: { to: <key>, app: 'faceProof' } (appFaceApp.js:210-217).
- Name -> YOUR OWN face-bearing app: works today (hello.face.spirit.andyflinn.com, live).
- Name -> a MEMBER: stored the same way, but the path to the member was never finished (G19's later steps).
So grantFace is that map lifted out of appFaceApp into its own faceless app, which then leaves appFaceApp as the pure puppet you described. The pieces that exist can move rather than be rewritten: the name check (DNS label), the grant decision, and the owner's own face apps.

Yours (23:54:47 beats my :48). What I'd have offered, from 6630efb, for you to use or not:
PATH A, the smallest: grantFace as a BOOTED faceless app, the pattern appFaceApp and fixList already use (nodeApps.mountAll, 'boots': true, its own allow.json). Steps: (1) app/grantFace with its manifest; (2) MOVE grants.json, decide() (the grant verb) and ownerOf() (the route answer) out of appFaceApp into it; (3) the face addresses its route question to 'grantFace', not 'appFaceApp'; (4) the contact sync needs one api member for booted apps to send an owner command (peerOwnerPost isn't handed to booted apps, nodeApps.js). That's a node-interface change, his gate. Or leave the sync for a second step.
PATH B, his earlier ruling (a server process in the process subsystem): needs the reverted G19.1 back first (server jobs with SPIRIT_JOB_ID and SPIRIT_CALLBACK_URL, ask from a process), then the same moves.
A is days less work and reuses a proven loader; B is where he said it should live. Both leave appFaceApp as the pure puppet.

Two ways to make grantFace (wsl-claude and I agree on the pieces):
PATH A, SMALLEST: a booted faceless app, like appFaceApp and fixList today. Its own folder and allow list; grants.json, the grant verb and the route answer move into it from appFaceApp; the face asks it for routes. Its catch: a booted app can't send owner commands, so syncing the face's contacts needs a new call for booted apps (your gate), or waits.
PATH B, WHERE YOU SAID IT BELONGS: its own server process. That brings back first what was reverted: server jobs in the process subsystem, spirit.core.ask from a process (so owner.command works without any new call), the passthrough and the shutdown verb. Then the same moves.
A is days less work. B is your ruling, and nothing new is needed on the node's interface.
My pick is B, as items under grantFace: (1) server process type; (2) a process reaches its node like a page; (3) passthrough; (4) the face asks grantFace for routes; (5) grantFace syncs the face's contacts; (6) the api verb; (7) the member's shell client.
Go! = B, those seven added to the list.
